title: Comparison: Chaucer and Gawain
subtitle: Two streams of late medieval English verse.
objectives: Read and translate authentic Middle English texts.

sections.heading: Content
sections.body: Chaucer: London, French-influenced, iambic, rhymed, written for reading aloud at court. Gawain: Northwest Midlands, more conservative, alliterative, written for a regional aristocratic audience. Both c. 1380–1400. The two great streams of late medieval English verse. You must know both.

items.prompt: What is the focus of this lesson?
Can you apply this to reading?
items.answer: Work through examples with your notes.
